description: Public hearing before Bluffdale City Redevelopment Agency (RDA) to consider a proposed boundary change for the Gateway Redevelopment Area. The proposal seeks to remove a portion of a city-owned open space parcel (approximately 0.10 acres or 4,384 square feet) from the redevelopment area. This adjustment would affect tax increment revenue allocation within the project area.
location: Bluffdale City Hall, 2222 W 14400 S; Parcel 33-09-201-020-0000

notes: Staff presenter: Ellen Oakman, Associate Planner. This is a regulatory/code amendment affecting tree standards citywide, not a specific development project. Likely low growth impact but important for infrastructure coordination.

notes: Staff presenter: Fred Donaldson. This is a regulatory/standards adoption affecting development in wildland-urban interface zones. May impact future development feasibility and construction costs in affected areas.

notes: Sign code amendment specific to gas station electronic display signage. Application 2026-10. Staff presenter: Ellen Oakman.

GRANTSVILLE CITY
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
FISCAL YEAR 2027 TENTATIVE BUDGET


PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Grantsville City Council will hold a Public Hearing on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of receiving public input regarding the proposed Fiscal Year 2027 Tentative Budget and the adoption of the tentative budget on an interim basis pending final budget adoption. 

The Grantsville City Council will also consider a Resolution declaring the City's intent to consider an increase in property tax revenue above the certified tax rate for Fiscal Year 2027 and establishing the date, time, and place of the future Truth in Taxation public hearing required by Utah Code Section 59-2-919.

The public hearing will be held in person at Grantsville City Hall, located at 429 E. Main Street, Grantsville, Utah, 84029, and electronically via Zoom.

Public comments are welcome and may be provided in person during the meeting, or electronically using the following information:

Meeting URL: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/4358843411
Dial-In: 1-253-215-8782
Meeting ID: 435 884 3411

Written comments may also be submitted to the City Recorder, Alicia Fairbourne, at afairbourne@grantsvilleut.gov. All written comments will be distributed to the City Council and entered into the public record. To ensure consideration, written comments must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) on the day of the meeting.

Copies of the proposed tentative budget, proposed resolution, and Property Tax Impact Schedule may be reviewed during regular business hours at Grantsville City Hall or online at: https://www.grantsvilleut.gov/transparency/public_notices.php#outer-18sub-382, or on the Utah Public Notice website at https://www.utah.gov/pmn/sitemap/publicbody/1840.html.

Spanish Fork City Council Notice to Spanish Fork City Utility Customers 2027
agenda_text:
NOTICE TO SPANISH FORK CITY UTILITY CUSTOMERS

State law requires that the City provide an annual disclosure on funds transferred from a utility enterprise fund to any other fund. The City has budgeted the following transfers. 

The City of Spanish Fork has budgeted for the transfer from each utility fund to the general fund as a dividend to Spanish Fork taxpayers. This dividend is the result of the rate payers' investment in the City's utility infrastructure. These funds are used each year to help cover costs of important city services like police, fire, library, senior center, parks and recreation, and other city functions. The utility transfer helps keep property taxes low in Spanish Fork. If City utility services were provided by private utility vendors, these dividends would instead be paid to the private investor-owners. Because Spanish Fork residents are the investor-owners, these dividends are used to offset what otherwise would be a significant increase in property tax rates. These transfers are of funds which cannot be defined as a reasonable allocation of costs between funds. These amounts will not be repaid. 

The amounts of the transfers are as follows:	Dollar Amount          	% of Expenditures 
From the Power Fund to the General Fund	$ 1,310,000	  3.3 % From the Water Fund to the General Fund 	$ 352,000		2.6 %

From the Solid Waste Fund to the General Fund 	$ 50,000 	 1.3 %

Spanish Fork City also has a debt obligation that the Power Fund is helping make payments on. The funds are to pay for the Justice Center (Police/Court Building).
